solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Aquatic creature — supply at sea: about a ton

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, that is around, the next pieces
something at sea is confused and adrift, so the letters of supply are jumbled

explanation.surface: A puzzling note about stocking a boat, tacked onto a mention of a water animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon splits the definition from the wordplay; 'at sea' is the anagram signal and 'about' puts A and T inside the jumble, not around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck-billed Australian mammal spends much of its life swimming in rivers, so it is a water-dwelling animal.

clue.text: Put down song as perceived by others?

parts.note: a lay is an old word for a ballad or song
to the rest means in the view of everyone else, so the phrase gives two words, to and rest

explanation.surface: Someone belittled a song, judging by how others heard it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' looks like criticise; here it means bury or end something for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean bury a body or settle a matter finally, an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: State: 'Times to invest in brewing products'

indicators.note: to invest is to put something into, so the times sign goes inside the brewed drinks

parts.note: teas are what you get by brewing leaves in hot water
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A headline: The Times newspaper decides to put money into a brewing company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign X; 'brewing products' is teas, not beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lone Star State is one of the fifty in the American union.

clue.text: One getting the sack maybe after us

parts.note: post is a Latin-derived prefix meaning after
man can stand for humankind, all of us

explanation.surface: Someone about to be fired, perhaps following the rest of us out of the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the sack' suggests dismissal; this carrier is handed a mailbag.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail carrier carries letters in a big sack on the round, so is one who gets one.

clue.text: Fight involving energy weapon

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the fight word wraps around the energy symbol

parts.note: to spar is to box or fight
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A bout of combat that uses an energy weapon, like a science-fiction battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance with a pointed head for throwing or thrusting is a classic hand weapon.

clue.text: Advantage in seed germination

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words seed germination, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A gardener's observation that some seeds sprout with a head start.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the upper hand over a rival is a synonym sense: a competitive lead.

clue.text: Fellow feeling making them pay, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among several, so the letters of them pay are reordered

explanation.surface: Feeling for others pushes someone to make them pay up, an ironic twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharing and understanding another person's emotions is sympathy, a synonym.

clue.text: Sentimentality is mostly beneficial

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: something beneficial is good for you

explanation.surface: A claim that a bit of soppiness generally does you good.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkish, sickly sentiment is informally called this sticky stuff, an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Cat associations reported on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard not seen, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: links are connections or associations

explanation.surface: Ties to a big cat mentioned in a radio report.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild cat with tufted ears and a short tail, an example of the feline family.

clue.text: Go, with speed, running round front of herd? One might

definitions.text: Go, with speed, running round front of herd? One might

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the next letter
running means set in motion and mixed, so go and speed are reordered
front of picks the first letter of herd

explanation.surface: Describes a working animal darting swiftly around the leading edge of a flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' is the anagram signal and 'round' puts the herd's first letter inside the jumble; read whole, the clue also describes the dog at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie or similar working breed trained to gather and drive flocks would dash around a herd like this.

clue.text: Someone eating ice-cream right to swallow everything

indicators.note: the cone takes in, or swallows, the total

parts.note: a cone is an ice-cream served in a wafer cornet
the sum is the total, everything

explanation.surface: A greedy diner wolfing down a whole ice-cream.
explanation.definitionFit: One who consumes food is an eater, the literal root sense of the word.

clue.text: Printing error: treaty gutted and work set back

indicators.note: a gutted word loses its insides, leaving its first and last letters
set back means turned round, so the work word is read backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A misprint ruined a treaty and delayed the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip at the keyboard or press is a misprint, a typographical mistake.

clue.text: Puritan, English, accepting detestable social advantage

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the prig and E wrap around the detestable word

parts.note: a prig is a self-righteous, puritanical person
vile means detestable

explanation.surface: A disapproving English puritan putting up with the hateful perks of class.
explanation.definitionFit: A special right or benefit enjoyed by a favoured few is a social advantage.

clue.text: See key in PE: one somehow to remain proficient

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A PE teacher's instruction: find the key to stay sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is physical education, the school sports lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from ball games, where regular practice keeps your skill sharp, so it means stay in practice.

clue.text: Grill family vegetable

parts.note: to pump someone is to grill them with questions
kin are your family

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction to grill the family's vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The big orange squash eaten in pies and soups is an example of a vegetable.

clue.text: Everyone in performance is superficial

indicators.note: the word for everyone goes inside the performance

parts.note: a show is a performance
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A critic sneering that the whole cast of a play is shallow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking depth of thought or feeling is a synonym sense, as in a skin-deep character.

clue.text: Thirteen letters identifying a small thing

definitions.text: Thirteen letters identifying a small thing

parts.words: Thirteen letters identifying a small thing
parts.note: the first thirteen letters of the alphabet run from A through to M, and written as a phrase that span names a tiny particle

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry: thirteen letters spell out a tiny object.
explanation.walkthrough: The first thirteen letters of the alphabet run from A to M.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest unit of a chemical element is a byword for something minutely tiny, and the alphabet span spells it.

clue.text: Leading institution marks joint suitable for replacement?

parts.note: flags are marks or markers set to note something
the hip is the joint most often replaced in surgery

explanation.surface: A hospital whose top unit marks patients for hip replacements.
explanation.walkthrough: A hip replacement is a common operation, hence 'suitable for replacement'.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally the admiral's ship, the word now means the leading or best example of an organisation.

clue.text: Father to admit a show of displeasure

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
to own up is to admit

explanation.surface: A priest owning up, with visible disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitting the brows is a facial expression showing disapproval.

clue.text: Brownish shade I included in copies, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection reverses an image, so the result is read backwards
the letter I is put inside the copies word

parts.note: to ape is to copy, so apes means copies

explanation.surface: An artist noting a brownish tint added to reproductions, seen in a mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' puts I inside APES to make APIES; 'on reflection' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: The reddish-brown tint of old photographs, named after cuttlefish ink, is a brownish colour.

clue.text: Give money to support two aerobatic manoeuvres

parts.note: a bank is a tilt of the wings, one of the two stunts named
a roll turns the aircraft over, the second of the two stunts

explanation.surface: Funding an air display with two stunt moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two' says the phrase supplies two manoeuvres side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To finance a venture is to fund it, the verb sense of providing the cash.

clue.text: Song from duo without piano

indicators.note: without means the piano letter is removed

parts.note: a duo is a pair
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: A song performed by a duo with no piano accompaniment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune or melody, especially a simple one, is a synonym for song.

clue.text: Statement in court sure to be overlooked in happiness

indicators.note: overlooked means left out, so sure is dropped from the happiness word

parts.note: pleasure is happiness

explanation.surface: A legal statement that is bound to be ignored amid general cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant's answer to the charge, guilty or not guilty, is a formal statement in court.

clue.text: Book featured healthy component of diet

parts.note: a story that ran in a paper was featured

explanation.surface: A diet book that highlighted a healthy ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal husks rich in fibre are a classic example of healthy roughage.

clue.text: Port not vintage? Have last of Semillon

parts.note: new is the opposite of vintage, not aged

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of Semillon

explanation.surface: A wine-list choice: this fortified wine is young, so have a Semillon instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine but is a harbour town; NEWHAVEN is a Channel ferry port in East Sussex, England. Semillon is a white grape.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Sussex town runs ferries to Dieppe, so it is an example of a seaport.
